budget_ms._comment: Budget for gate path [sys.executable, script] — no shell, real Python. During active OneDrive sync + Defender scanning, startup alone consumes 1700ms+. Values are p90 syncing-state gate-path totals observed 2026-09-23. Production path (shell=True) runs 1.8x slower — see FACTS.md §11.

_comment_interpreter_floor: Measured 2026-09-23 on Windows 11 / OneDrive (<org>) / Python 3.14.3. Method: subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', 'pass']). States: (1) quiet/idle: p50=534ms. (2) active OneDrive sync: p50=1707ms. (3) OneDrive paused (sync paused from tray): p50=1333ms — filter driver overhead persists even when sync is paused, because the driver intercepts file reads regardless of sync state. Running hook scripts from OneDrive costs ~5s additional when Defender scans the script file on first read — 6580ms gate-path vs 1333ms floor. Defender path exclusions (hooks-dir + Lib) reduce this to 1132ms during active sync (-37%). See FACTS.md §11.
_comment_kill_switch_headroom: Added to interpreter_floor_ms to get kill_threshold. 800ms covers stdlib imports (json/os/sys) plus Defender scan headroom. Total: floor(1700) + headroom(800) = 2500ms.
_comment_daemon_trigger: Thresholds for the Phase 4 daemon decision. The daemon is justified if Stop hooks are being KILLED often enough to lose real memories — not because a millisecond number crosses an arbitrary line. Primary metric: stop_drop_rate_pct from hook_log (Stop events / UserPromptSubmit events). Secondary: duration_warn_ms for within-Python DB perf. min_hook_events: don't trigger recommendations until there's enough data.

daemon_trigger._comment_stop_drop_warn: Stop/UPS ratio below (100 - 2)% → warn that candidates are being lost. Rationale: 1 in 50 turns is the pain threshold — occasional spikes are noise; persistent 2%+ means the timeout is too tight for the machine. Threshold set 2026-09-23 BEFORE real data; revisit after 50+ real sessions.
daemon_trigger._comment_stop_drop_daemon: Stop/UPS ratio below 95% over 50+ events → recommend daemon. Rationale: 1 in 20 turns losing a candidate is unacceptable for a memory tool. At this rate the cost of the daemon (implementation complexity, IPC overhead) is clearly justified. Set before real data; revisit after 50+ sessions.
daemon_trigger._comment_duration_warn: hook_log.duration_ms p50 above this → DB or retrieval is unusually slow (separate from spawn cost). Normal within-Python work is 50-100ms; 200ms suggests a problem.
daemon_trigger._comment_min_events: Minimum hook_log entries (across both Stop and UserPromptSubmit) before drop-rate recommendations fire. Raised from 20 to 50 — need a real week of sessions to distinguish a fluke spike from a structural problem.
daemon_trigger._removed_spawn_thresholds: spawn_warn_ms and spawn_daemon_ms removed 2026-09-23. Those thresholds were set against the broken state (5s timeout, unoptimised commands) and were already tripped before the cheap fixes landed. Daemon justification is about lost data, not spawn latency.
